sources.title: Dev versus Delta: Demystifying engineering roles at Palantir

facts.claim: Palantir positions its platforms as serving organizations across public, private, and non-profit sectors.
facts.quote: Our platforms are used throughout the public, private, and non-profit sectors to help organizations quickly implement solutions to the hardest problems they face.

facts.claim: Palantir markets an Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning offering for enterprises.
facts.quote: Consequential AI for the modern enterprise.

facts.claim: Palantir markets a Defense offering spanning land, air, sea, and space operations.
facts.quote: A tactical edge — by land, air, sea, and space.

facts.claim: Palantir's official careers guidance says candidates should narrate their approach and ask clarifying questions during technical interviews.
facts.quote: When presented with analytical and technical problems, talk through how you plan to approach the problem and ask questions if necessary.

facts.claim: Palantir's Software Engineers ("Devs") build the Foundry and Gotham platforms.
facts.quote: Devs (Software Engineers) develop and engineer our software platforms, Palantir Foundry and Palantir Gotham.

facts.claim: Palantir's Forward Deployed Software Engineers ("Deltas") deploy the platforms directly to customers.
facts.quote: Deltas (Forward Deployed Software Engineers) deploy our software platforms to customers.

facts.claim: Palantir describes the Ontology as the core of the Foundry platform.
facts.quote: The Foundry Ontology is the heart of Palantir Foundry.

facts.claim: Palantir's official careers guidance says interview attire is casual and not evaluated.
facts.quote: we're a laid-back company, so wear whatever you feel most comfortable in

facts.claim: Palantir describes Foundry as an ontology-powered operating system for the modern enterprise.
facts.quote: The Ontology-Powered Operating System for the Modern Enterprise

signals.text: Frame JD-relevant enterprise AI/ML or cross-sector operational platform experience around Palantir's stated focus on public, private, and non-profit sector platforms and enterprise AI, when the candidate's own evidence supports it.
When JD coverage and claim safety are equal for a Defense-scoped role, prefer the supported bullet demonstrating operationally reliable or mission-critical systems work.
Note in G3 advisory that Palantir's own interview guidance recommends narrating your approach and asking clarifying questions during technical interview rounds.

Frame end-to-end platform component ownership (e.g., data infrastructure or semantic-layer work) around Palantir's description of Devs owning platform components end-to-end, when supported by the candidate's own evidence.
When JD coverage and claim safety are equal for a Foundry-scoped role, prefer the supported bullet demonstrating semantic or ontology-driven data system design.
Note in G3 advisory that Palantir's official careers guidance states interview attire is casual and not evaluated; this never changes the renderer or L7 rules.
